body:
> This will not compile :).

And IMO this is the intention as you can only query for:
* names (type: `string`)
* directive instance type (type: `Type|Function`)

See: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/core/src/metadata/di.ts#L295

Not sure what you are trying to achieve, but the current typing is intentional.

Well if it is intentional, then see recomended solution for https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12758 by @tbosch  and tell me how can you do it? 

What im trying to do is get all components that inherits from super class, it is exactly what that issue mentioned above is talking about. 

If you want to have dynamic content and you have base class and then 2 various components that inherits from that base class and you want to get via `ViewChildren` or `ContentChildren` all components that inherits from that base class that is only way to do it. 

Funny thing is if it is intentional, so why it is working? When you ignore types and use `any` it works.

You can query for a type instead of `InjectionToken`: http://plnkr.co/edit/S5k0c28x0j5lmfEOoRGE?p=preview

In any case, I think that there is a discrepancy here between _intention_ and _implementation_ in place.

I'm also confused by that.
Why does view queries are restricted to type token ? 

I can imagine 2 reasons for that : 

1) it's by design, then I'm failing to see why we would want that.
2) it's a constraint due to implementation, but as op said and I could also experienced it, it totally works if you go around the typings. Maybe it's an old restriction that doesn't apply anymore ?

Using an empty class as a token instead of an `InjectionToken` to get around this feels like a silly typing workaround.

I have `BaseClass`, then i have `MyComponentClass` and `MyComponentClass2`. Both of these classes extends `BaseClass` and have `Component` decorator.

Now i have this html template.

```html
<my-component1></my-component1>
<my-component2></my-component2>
```

How can i query those 2 components implementations in `ViewChildren` in single property? I dont care about concrete implementation, because everything i need is defined in `BaseClass`.

If i use `ViewChildren(BaseClass)` it will not work, it returns empty `QueryList` so i cant use type. Only solution that works and i repeat this again is using `InjectionToken` (as recommended by @tbosch) where it is used as `ExistanceProvider` with multi value which is Provided by `MyComponentClass` and `MyComponentClass2` component providers.

So tell me how can i get all different implementations of `BaseClass` in single `QueryList` if it does not does not work while querying `BaseClass` and i should not use `InjectionToken` even if it is working?

Thank you :)

Ok sorry, i have open your plunker and i see what you mean. Ok it is possible to use type for this, but i still think it is misuse of "fictional" class created. I think `InjectionToken` was created exactly for this purpose, otherwise we could have always use some dummy class and use it instead of `InjectionToken`.

In a complex application, your component could already be extending a class but still want to _implement_ and _provide_ a small interface shared by many components. In this situation you would need this `@ViewChildren(MY_INJECTION_TOKEN)` feature. Without this feature, you'd have to do a painful refactor and make all the components extend the same class even if it doesn't make sense for your design.

**Current Solution Tip**
Since no one has mentioned it, when  `MyComponent extends BaseClass`, you also need to **provide** BaseClass:

In **my-component.ts**'s  `@Component({providers: ...})`
```typescript
    { provide: BaseClass, useExisting: forwardRef(() => MyComponent)},
```

- BaseClass can be abstract
- Not sure if provide line should have `multi: true`

I was very surprised to find it doesn't work and what is even stranger is it does indeed work if you write it like that:
`@ContentChild(MY_TOKEN as any) something: SuperClass;`
Please fix this as it is scary to use like that.

issue.title: @ViewChild(MyInjectorToken as any, { static: false }) no longer works with Ivy

issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package Ivy Compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes. This used to work with Angular 8 ### Description To get view children or content children that implement a certain abstract class or interface requires a bit of a workaround - casting the injector token to "any" - but was definitely supported in so far that somebody had to have written the code that deals with the injector token. For details, see the related issues: * https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12758 * https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/21152 With a new Angular 9 (9.0.0-rc.5) project, the same mechanism fails in the AOT compillation step with the message: "error TS-991010: @ViewChild predicate cannot be interpreted" ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-viewchildtoken-angular8-4dpwkt?file=src%2Fapp%2Fhello.component.ts 1. Download the Stackblitz sample 2. Upgrade the project to Angular 9 rc5 with `ng update --next=true @angular/cli @angular/core` 3. Build the project in AOT mode ## 🔥 Exception or Error 

error TS-991010: @ViewChild predicate cannot be interpreted
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 9.0.0-rc.5
Node: 10.16.0
OS: win32 x64

Angular: 9.0.0-rc.5
... animations, cli, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... language-service, platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic
... router
Ivy Workspace: Yes

Package                            Version
------------------------------------------------------------
@angular-devkit/architect          0.900.0-rc.5
@angular-devkit/build-angular      0.900.0-rc.5
@angular-devkit/build-ng-packagr   0.900.0-rc.5

@ngtools/webpack                   9.0.0-rc.5
@schematics/angular                9.0.0-rc.5
@schematics/update                 0.900.0-rc.5

rxjs                               6.5.3
typescript                         3.6.4
webpack                            4.41.2
*Edit*: A fellow developer had some trouble to reproduce the issue, so think it's worth mention that the error only appears when building in AOT mode.

body: Agree that we should adjust types since it is an useful pattern which works in practice. At this point the only thing that is broken are types, really. Confirming as a bug.
